subject: ancientTreant
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: ancient treant, walking tree guardian.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a biped treant model, roughly 4.2 meters tall, with a bark trunk body, root-like legs, branch arms, a glowing-eyed face set into the trunk, and a foliage crown decorated with moss, mushrooms, and glowing runes, aiming for a moderate-length, well-structured module around 400 lines.

I'm mapping out the skeleton—hips, spine chain, chest, neck, head, jaw, shoulders with hanging arm limbs, and leg limbs down to rooted feet with spread toe digits—then setting up bark paint using noise-based grain and mottle with moss on upward-facing surfaces, plus textures for glowing eyes, runes, leaves, and moss tufts. Writing the loft-based body and head geometry...

Working out the finger chains with tapered digits off the wrist tip, then moving to the legs using the same limb-based point chains for hips downward.

I'm adding bark knots scattered on the torso, moss patches on the shoulders filtered by upward-facing normals, and mushroom caps with glowing orange spots placed along the body. I'm also planning a glowing rune decal on the chest, and making sure the feet and toe geometry sit flush with the ground plane at the right radii and heights.

Now I'm working out eye placement on the skull sphere as a decal with a glowing amber slit texture, positioned near the front surface, and starting to think through the brow and nose shapes.

For the mouth, I'm planning a dark gap decal on the jaw with the jaw itself modeled as a scaled sphere joined to the skull, plus a couple of small fang cones for detail. The head sits atop the trunk at the right width, and I'm starting to lay out crown foliage as flattened icosahedron blobs arranged around the upper head with branches sweeping up from the skull top.

Now I'm choosing a nature-themed palette of bark, moss, leaf greens, and amber glow tones, and writing the bark paint function that mixes dark and tan browns with noise-based grain streaks and moss blending based on surface normal.

Next I'm setting up the body's loft stations, defining width and height at several heights from hips to shoulders to create a tapering, chest-forward torso shape, and thinking through how to bind this to the spine and hip bones.

Then I'm working out the spine chain as four points rising from hips to neck with a slight forward curve, assigning the chest joint, and attaching the head and jaw joints with proper parenting and aim targets. I'm placing the shoulder joints symmetrically on the chest bone, positioning them to sit correctly within the torso loft, and planning to add mossy bark-knot pauldrons and scattered bark plate cones as surface detail on the torso and shoulders.

Still placing shoulder mushrooms, then adding hanging beard roots from the jaw as catmull sweeps, and a glowing spiral rune decal on the chest surface using a projected texture. Time to finalize everything.
